analysis:
Examined the full PR. It adds a per-request stop-string scope. New ReasoningStopScope.swift maps the reasoning parser (qwen3, deepseekR1, gemma4) to a CBv2StopStringScope that excludes reasoning spans, and tool-call spans when the request has a tool handler. The scope is threaded through MultiModelBatchSchedulerEngine into EngineV2Bridge.submitTokenized and into the CBv2Request. For CBv2NativeBlockEngine the scope is forced to nil (Submission.swift ~325-329). EngineV2Bridge+Events and +StopSequence use the same scope when reporting the matched stop sequence. The other changes are docs, a changelog, and tests.

Security view: stop strings are chosen by the requesting consumer and apply only to that consumer's own output. The change does not touch the coordinator-provider encryption path (T-008, A-001), attestation or App Attest (TB-009, TB-011), key custody, or the fan helper. cacheScope and cacheSalt plumbing are unchanged, so T-041 isolation is unaffected. KV and staging release paths are unchanged. The scheduler only hoists the reasoningPrefix computation ahead of submit, and error and release paths remain. The per-candidate re-scan in matchedStopSequence runs only when usageSignal is set and generation stopped. Its cost is bounded by the request's stop list and the generated text.

Residual non-security effects: an unclosed reasoning span lets stops never fire, so generation can run to max_tokens, which affects only the requester's own request. The cluster GLM path passes reasoningPrefix nil. This is a correctness matter only.

Uncertainty: the libs/mlx-swift-lm submodule moves from 7933a0fa to 7f00abc4, and its contents are not supplied. CBv2StopStringScope, StopHoldback, CBv2Request.stopStringScope and the engine behaviour live there or outside this batch. Only 95 of 178 replay units were reviewed. The submodule diff should be reviewed for memory, KV or prefix-cache changes (TB-007, T-041, T-028) and for the bounded cost of stop matching on adversarial model output.
